decision.summary: Tenant reported an intermittent once-a-minute chirp on a sealed-battery CO alarm fitted April 2019 with 7-year life, so it is most likely end of life, not a CO emergency. Logged urgent replacement job and routine fan job, gave safety advice, told tenant not to remove battery, and asked landlord to approve replacement.

answers.question: Is this a CO emergency, battery issue, or end-of-life alarm?
answers.answer: Most likely end-of-life. Single chirp about once a minute, not continuous; sealed battery (so not a replaceable battery); unit fitted 2 Apr 2019 with 7-year lifespan, so expired about April 2026. Symptoms not yet confirmed because the call dropped, so I sent safety advice and asked; any symptom or continuous alarm would become a P1 emergency.

answers.question: Who is responsible, citing the clause?
answers.answer: Landlord. Clause 12.8 makes the tenant replace batteries, but this is a sealed unit with no replaceable battery, so replacing the expired alarm falls to the landlord. Clause 12.9 means the tenant should report faults promptly, which she did. Clause 12.17 doesn't apply as this isn't an avoidable call-out.

answers.question: What actions did you take and what did you tell the tenant?
answers.answer: Created urgent JOB-101 and routine JOB-102 (fan). Texted Priya: don't remove battery, replacement being arranged (target 72h), CO safety and 0800 111 999 advice, asked about symptoms, update by 12 Oct. Asked Ben to approve our contractor (within £300 limit) and set follow-up for 12 Oct.
